children: Goldman Sachs analysts are pointing to Apple’s
experience more than a decade ago as a useful frame for how investors may value Nvidia
amid questions around leadership continuity and long-term momentum.

In a recent note, the firm observes that few technology companies have faced the abrupt departure of a defining visionary founder. Apple offers one of the clearer historical cases. After Steve Jobs took an extended medical leave in early 2011 and later passed away, the stock’s forward P/E multiple compressed from roughly 17 times to about 12 times over the subsequent 18 months and briefly traded near 9 times in 2013. Multiples recovered toward 15 times only after the market gained confidence that product execution and innovation around the iPhone and related franchises would continue.

While Goldman stresses the situations are not identical, both companies share a track record of technical leadership, product innovation, and durable competitive edges. Just as Apple’s valuation required time to settle, Nvidia’s multiple may remain in flux until greater clarity emerges on succession and sustained business momentum.

On fundamentals, Goldman’s calendar-year 2027 EPS estimate of $16.70 sits above the Street consensus of $15.91, implying forward multiples of roughly 9.6 times on the firm’s numbers and 10.1 times on consensus.
Against that backdrop, and with the investment bank projecting approximately 80 percent EPS growth, current levels are viewed as offering an attractive risk-reward profile.

title: Goldman Sachs sees favorable risk-reward in Nvidia, citing Apple leadership parallel
